target_customer: Brazilian creators and influencers who sell courses, memberships and paid communities
problem: Influencers who sold access to closed WhatsApp and Telegram groups had no easy way to charge and manage members. ChatPay handled payments for them and later became a full creator commerce platform.
business_model: Payments take rate on creator sales (PIX, card, boleto) plus platform features

founders.name: Arthur Alvarenga
founders.background_notes: YC page: software engineer with product design experience. Bloomberg Linea and Startups.com.br name him CEO or president.

founders.name: Breno Oliveira
founders.background_notes: YC page: in product and software development since 1993.

founders.name: Bernardo Reis
founders.background_notes: YC page: Android developer with server side Kotlin, Java and Python experience.

founders.name: Raphael Capelão
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio.

competitors.name: Hotmart
competitors.what: Brazilian digital product and creator platform with payments and affiliate tools
competitors.traction_then: Described as a unicorn since March 2020 and bought Teachable, Wollo and Klickpages in 2020
competitors.funding_then: Reported US$130M Series C in 2021; valuation above $1B per CB Insights

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments (PIX, card, boleto), recurring billing and chat app group management integrations; standard fintech engineering with several Brazilian payment methods.

defensibility.rationale: Many Brazilian infoproduct platforms existed. Creator audiences and payment history create modest lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept scaling and none acquired Hubla as far as found; Hubla repositioned broadly in November 2021.

market_need_then: Creators sold access to WhatsApp and Telegram groups and needed billing tools. Startups.com.br described ChatPay as managing payments for influencers running closed groups.

branding.name_origin: Hubla combines hub, meaning group or community, with bla, a nod to voice and conversation (Startups.com.br, November 2021).
branding.domain_note: Uses hub.la, a short domain hack, which redirects to lp.hub.la.

identity.voice_and_tone: Creator focused slogans such as Shopify for creators.

rebrands.why: Repositioning to give creators more than payments, announced with the Series A.

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The rebrand received Brazilian business press and the new name suits the broader creator platform, but no sources show brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Payments for influencers' closed WhatsApp and Telegram groups (ChatPay)
pivots.to: All-in-one creator platform for courses, communities and memberships (Hubla)
pivots.why: To offer creators more features and build for the future of work, per the rebrand announcement.

outcome_analysis: ChatPay raised about $2.1 million in 2020 and in November 2021 renamed itself Hubla and raised R$60 million in a Series A led by Kaszek. The pivot from group payments to a full creator platform rode the Brazilian infoproduct boom, and YC lists a team of about 100 and Active status. No later rounds were found, so the growth story rests on the 2021 round and company claims.
notes: The directory slug is chatpay and the company is now Hubla. The Series A is R$60M, about US$10.8M per Bloomberg Linea. The seed was reported as 2020 US$2.1M; one aggregator lists a 2019 seed, which conflicts. The Hotmart source is dated April 2021, about nine months after the batch, so it is a weaker as-of source; it describes 2020 events. The seed label comes from Brazil Journal via a search summary; Startups.com.br gives the amount and investors without a label. Aggregator totals conflict (CB Insights $10.81M, ZoomInfo $10M, Caplight $13.05M). Hubla website redirected and was not read in detail. No acquisition or layoff news found.
